transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I'm just having some issues with... getting things done, I guess. I keep losing chunks of time lately. 

I just end up re-reading my emails and texts a lot, or... reopening folders on my computer. And before I leave the house or start work, I just get stuck mentally replaying conversations. It's... I don't know, it's like I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. 

So... yeah, that's why I'm here.
Can you describe what goes through your mind when you're re-reading emails or replaying conversations? Are you feeling anxious, or is it more like you can't stop thinking about it?

I suppose it's... it's more that I just can't stop thinking about it. I'll be trying to work, you know, going through a system design or... preparing a lesson, and this thought just barges in. 

It's usually something like... maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife. Or that I somehow mishandled some family photos, or... let someone in the community down. I don't know. Even though I know I've already been over it, I just... I can't seem to let it pass.
Do these thoughts feel like they don’t belong to you or that they go against what you believe or want to think about?
No, they... they definitely feel like my thoughts. I just... I don't want to be having them. But they're mine.

When these thoughts come up, do you feel like you have to do something — like re-read messages, check things repeatedly, or go through a mental ritual — to make the anxiety go away or to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah... like I mentioned before, I guess. That's... that's when I end up re-reading the emails and texts. Or reopening those folders on my computer. 

I just feel like I have to do it. Like I have to mentally replay the conversations before I can leave the house or start my work. Just to... prove to myself I didn't make some serious mistake. So... yes. I guess I do feel like I have to do it.
Do these thoughts and the things you do to manage them interfere with your daily life, like your work, relationships, or other important activities?

I guess... yes. It does get in the way. 

My work has slowed down quite a bit. I've actually... missed some design milestones recently. And I've had to postpone a few mentoring sessions that I usually handle without any trouble. I just... couldn't get to them. 

And, well... I help out with a youth coding workshop. It matters a lot to me, but... I showed up late the other day. I was completely unprepared. It was... pretty embarrassing, to be honest. I don't really like thinking about that part. But yes, I suppose it interferes.
When you're trying to resist these thoughts or stop yourself from re-reading emails and folders, does it cause you a lot of distress or anxiety?

I don't... I haven't really tried to just stop myself. Not completely. So I'm not sure if I'd call it distress. 

It's just... uncomfortable, I guess. It's usually just easier to check the folders and get it over with rather than try to fight it. So I don't really know.
When you feel the urge to re-read emails or replay conversations, and you try to resist doing it, does it cause you noticeable anxiety or discomfort?

I think... I think you just asked me that. Like I said, I haven't really tried to stop myself. It's just... easier to just do it. So I don't really know how much anxiety it would cause if I didn't. I just do it.
Are there times when these thoughts feel especially intrusive or unwanted, and do you try to push them out of your mind or do something else to distract yourself from them?

I suppose they are unwanted, yes. Like... I'll be right in the middle of working through a system design, or trying to prepare a lesson for the kids, and... a thought just barges in. 

Just... things about my personal life. Like maybe I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or... mishandled some family photos. Or that I let someone in the community down. 

I try to just focus on my work to push it out, but... I can't seem to let it pass. Even when I know I've already been over it. It just... stays there.

When you have these thoughts, do you feel like you have to perform these repetitive actions—like re-reading emails or replaying conversations—to prevent something bad from happening or to make the anxiety go away?

I suppose so... yes. It's why I came in, really. I just... I keep losing chunks of time doing it. 

I'll sit there re-reading emails and texts, or... reopening folders on my computer. Mentally replaying conversations over and over before I can even leave the house or start my work. 

I don't know if I think something bad will happen, exactly. It's more like... I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. Once I check, the feeling settles down a bit. Until the next time.
When you re-read emails or replay conversations in your mind, is it mainly to reduce your anxiety or to make sure that something bad doesn’t happen as a result of a mistake you might have made?
I think... I just answered that, didn't I? It's... mostly to settle the feeling. To make sure I didn't mess something up. Like I just said.

When you re-read emails or replay conversations, is it mainly to prevent or reduce the anxiety you feel, or is it more about trying to make sure something bad doesn’t happen because of a mistake you might have made?

I... I don't really know how else to explain it. We just went over this. 

I just... I do it so the feeling goes away. That's all. I don't really have anything else to add to that.
Do you feel that these thoughts or the things you do to manage them, like re-reading emails or replaying conversations, are excessive or unreasonable?

I suppose so... yes. It's why I'm here. 

I just... I'm losing too much time to it. Hours, sometimes, just sitting there going over the same emails, or opening and closing folders... going over things in my head before I can even get to work. 

So, yes. I know it's excessive. I just... I can't seem to stop checking to make sure I didn't mess up.
Do you feel that the things you do, like re-reading emails or replaying conversations, are meant mainly to prevent or reduce your anxiety or to keep something bad from happening?

I... Doctor, you keep asking me this. I really don't know what else to tell you. 

I just do it to make the feeling stop. I don't have a different answer for you.
When you re-read emails or replay conversations, is it mainly to stop feeling anxious or to make sure that something bad doesn’t happen because of something you might have done wrong?

Doctor, I... we've been over this. I don't... I don't know why you're asking me the exact same thing again. 

I told you, I do it to make the feeling go away. I just... I keep losing chunks of time doing it. Re-reading the emails, texts... opening and closing folders... going over conversations in my head before I can even start my work. 

I just... I'm trying to prove to myself I didn't make some serious mistake. That's all. I don't know what else to say.
When you re-read emails or replay conversations, is it because you're trying to prevent something specific from happening, like a misunderstanding or a mistake with real consequences?

Yes. Like I just said. I'm trying to prove to myself I didn't make some serious mistake. 

That's why I came in... because I keep losing chunks of time to this. Re-reading the texts and emails, reopening folders, replaying the conversations in my head before I leave the house or start my work. 

I... I really don't know how many different ways I can answer this for you.
Is the main reason you re-read emails or replay conversations to neutralize the anxiety you feel, or is it more about preventing a specific feared event or consequence?
I... I think I've answered this. I don't know what you want me to say. I just do it to stop the feeling and make sure I didn't mess up. That's it.
